subject: gargoyle
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: cathedral gargoyle crouched on a ledge.
Style: gothic stone carving.
reasoning:
I'll keep the scope manageable, around 150 parts with a few textures, designing a gargoyle crouched on a ledge with haunches, spine, chest, neck, and head positioned forward, wings folded behind, and arms planted on the stone ledge.

I'm laying out joint coordinates for the ledge slab, hips, spine chain, neck chain, and head, then planning separate chain sweeps for spine and neck with a tail chain curling along the ledge.

I'm now sketching the hind leg geometry, computing hip-to-foot distances for the limb function with knee bending forward, and checking the segment lengths stay within reach.

Next I'm placing the arms with shoulder and hand coordinates, checking the reach distance against limb lengths, and deciding the elbows should bend outward and back to give the gargoyle a more hunched, clawed posture.

Then I'm moving to the head: building the skull from scaled sphere/box shapes with a separate jaw joint, adding curved backward-sweeping horns, pointed ears, brow ridges, and stone-carved eyes using textured planes with pupil details.

Continuing the lower jaw to extend forward with narrowing widths, attached to the jaw bone. I'm adding fang spikes jutting up from the lower jaw and down from the upper, then planning to pose the jaw open about 15 degrees on the x-axis at the end, after all parts are built, since posing after construction rotates everything correctly. I confirm the head-local coordinate helper returns proper vectors for joint placement, and move on to planning the horns.

For horns, I'm sweeping a bezier curve from a head-local point offset to the side and up, using a sign variable to mirror left/right, with a backward-curving control point attached to the head bone. For ears, I'm skipping standard rounded ears in favor of flat, pointed bat-style ear shapes extruded from a small leaf-like outline positioned on the side of the head, thin in the front-back direction so they read as flat cards facing forward, mirrored for the opposite side. Now I'm starting to think through how the wings should fold against the body.

Now I'm working out positions for the gargoyle's spread wings, placing shoulder joints near the top of the back and building out arm-like chains through elbow, wrist, and finger bones that fan outward and backward, then settling on a half-spread pose with wrist and three fingertip points positioned to create a natural bat-wing silhouette, with membrane surfaces stretched between the finger chains and down to the body edge.

Adding a thumb spike at the wrist, giving the wing membrane a slightly lighter stone paint, and considering a small rune emblem decal on the ledge front for texture.

I'm narrowing textures down to around four or five: an eye, a quatrefoil carving, a tracery arch relief on the ledge, and maybe a moss tuft card. For the stone paint I'm defining custom mottled grey tones with moss accents on upward faces and dark soot streaks for weathering.

Writing ledge and body paint logic...

I'm setting hips as the root joint at the base of the spine, then building the neck as a chain extending from the spine's end with tapering sweep radii, and attaching the head joint as its child.

Working out the spine point coordinates so the neck's starting position matches the spine's endpoint, accounting for the gargoyle's hunched, crouching pose with raised haunches above the ledge, then placing the head's final position and orientation at the top of the neck.

Now I'm working through the shoulder joint placement, offsetting it from the spine to account for chest width, then building the arm chain from shoulder to elbow to wrist with the hand positioned forward and down, checking the resulting limb segment distances come out reasonable.

For the elbow bend, I'm choosing a hint direction that angles the joint outward and back to get a natural bend. Then I'm adding the hand's paw shape with small claw spikes projecting forward from the hand point.

Now I'm working on the legs, placing the clawed hindfoot and a haunch sphere at the hip-knee midpoint bound to the first leg joint, then moving to facial details like brow ridges and eye decals mapped onto the skull sphere.

I'm calculating the eye decal placement and direction, checking that it projects correctly onto the forward-facing surface of the skull sphere so the carved stone eyeball with its slit pupil sits properly within the sphere's extents.

Now I'm working out how to snap the eye decal onto the actual skull surface using an azimuth/elevation projection from the skull center, with a fallback for when the hit test returns null. I'm also planning the brow as a curved rod sweeping from near the eye upward and outward across the head.

Then I'm sketching the facial details: a nose piece on the muzzle tip with nostrils, an upper jaw/lip box, downward fangs from the upper jaw and upward tusk-like fangs from the lower jaw using directional vectors, plus a jaw joint aimed toward a forward point on the head. I'm skipping the tongue but adding a small goatee spike under the chin and considering spike-based cheek ruffs.

Now I'm planning the mane as a row of blade-like spikes along the neck sweep, and designing a stone ledge object made of layered boxes (base slab, cornice moulding, top lip) attached to the hips bone, with moss/tuft texture cards scattered across upward-facing surfaces and an arched quatrefoil relief plane on the ledge's front face.

I'm working out the ledge's depth and position so claws can curl naturally over its front edge, and tracing a curved path for the tail so it drapes down along the back of the ledge with tapering radius toward the tip.

Simplifying the tail tip to a pointed spike instead, with ridge spikes running along the tapered tail, then moving on to shaping the haunch and thigh.

Working out hip and leg joint positions, foot placement sinking onto the ledge surface, and the low paw box for toes. I'm assigning stone textures per body part, with darker tones for horns and claws, lighter teeth, moss accents, and considering a faint ember glow for the eyes despite the stone material.

I decide to add a subtle amber glow to the eye slits using the glow kit, designing an almond-shaped eye texture with a dark outline, radial amber fill, and dark slit pupil. Then I move to detailing the wing membranes with finger sweeps, tears, and double-sided material, and start defining the wing arm chain geometry.

Writing wing bone chains...

I'm thinking about decorative tracery for the ledge front with quatrefoil outlines in muted grays, and considering adding a sigil or glyph motif on the chest as an identifying mark.

Now I'm planning moss tuft decoration scattered on the ledge top and shoulders using green blade cards, then thinking about additional texture details like dorsal ridge spikes, elbow knuckle spurs, and small dark nostril spheres to add more character.

I'm now defining the paint colors for stone, teeth, claws, and horns using mottled textures, then building out the head geometry—skull sphere, muzzle frustum, and nose box—positioned relative to the head bone with careful attention to scale and orientation.

Now I'm working out the lower jaw as a frustum shape anchored to a jaw bone aimed toward the head, checking that the jaw and muzzle dimensions taper correctly and leave a believable gap between upper and lower jaw.

I'm positioning the upper and lower fang spikes relative to the head and jaw bones, computing their base offsets, directions, and sizes so they sit along the jawline correctly, then starting on the cheek spikes.

Now I'm defining the horn curves using quadratic bezier paths swept with tapering thickness and flat caps, anchored to the head bone with horn coloring, before moving on to shaping the ears via extrusion.

Actually I decide ears would crowd the horn geometry, so I skip them and rely on horns plus brow detailing instead. For the neck I'll sweep a maned ridge with small spikes, and inside the mouth I'm adding a dark reddish-gray tongue frustum between the jaws for interior detail, plus considering a darker eye socket recess.

Writing hand and finger geometry...

Defining leg and arm chains...

Now I'm working out the ledge geometry: a base box with a top lip sitting above it, keeping the lowest point at y=0. I'm adding a row of small dentil blocks beneath the front of the lip, spaced across x, then merging them into one group.

For the front face, I'm placing a plane with tracery texture tinted in muted grays to match the carved relief look, and I'll reuse a stretched version for the side faces, adjusting the repeating quatrefoil pattern so it doesn't look elongated.

Now I'm positioning the front and side planes with their orientation axes, then moving to other textures: a mossy tuft decal with green blade paths, and a chest sigil using a circle-and-cross motif rendered in dark stroke on a muted fill.

I'm placing the eye decals using hit normals for direction and sizing them to match the eye texture's aspect ratio, then adding dorsal ridge spikes and pelvis geometry to round out the mesh.

Now I'm positioning the jaw's final pose rotation, working out the wing membrane thickness, and verifying that limb polylines use proper Vector3 arrays. I'm also placing foot pads and toe segments with specific offsets, radii, and directions to match the paw silhouette.

I'm defining the body sweep radius function so the profile narrows at the hips, widens at the chest, then tapers again toward the tail, with a separate neck radius for a smooth transition into the head. Then I move on to writing the sweep sections with stone-like coloring.
